request.outcome: The first baseline achieved 151/160 complete uninterrupted successes (94.375%) on the held-out official target distribution. Failures were dominated by transient boundary regulation: 6/9 failures never entered the 1 cm tolerance, with minimum distances near the boundary (mean 0.98 cm), and the 3/9 that entered immediately lost the hold after only 1-2 sampled steps with post-entry overshoot of 0.19-0.55 cm. Failure rates were similar across radius bands (5.0% at 6-10 cm, 5.7% at 10-14 cm, 5.1% at 14-18 cm, and 7.1% at 18-20 cm), so the current 0.06-0.14 m coverage gap is not the dominant explanation. Hold interruptions contribute but are secondary: they occurred in 3/9 failures, and no failure entered and then remained uninterrupted without completing. I1 therefore identifies transient reach/braking and boundary regulation as the next intervention target.
request.reason: T1 and M1 satisfy the closure condition with a trained baseline and phase-specific official-distribution diagnostics. Remaining uncertainty about how to improve the transient is consequential for the next inquiry, but further I1 measurement is not needed to choose that direction.

request.outcome: I2 found that the tested boundary-aware braking intervention did not improve complete uninterrupted success; it destroyed approach competence under the controlled training budget. On the shared held-out official-distribution panel, T2:checkpoint-120832 achieved 0/160 successes versus T1:checkpoint-100352 at 151/160, with paired candidate wins 0, reference wins 151, and net wins -151. T2 never entered the 1 cm tolerance in any episode: first entry and post-entry overshoot were therefore undefined, longest uninterrupted in-tolerance streak was 0 steps in all 160 episodes, and interruptions were 0 because no hold was initiated. Its mean minimum distance was 9.48 cm (median 7.13 cm), compared with T1's 0.278 cm mean (median 0.221 cm); T1 entered in 154/160 episodes, with mean first entry at 13.1 steps, mean longest streak 94.4 steps, mean post-entry overshoot 0.011 cm among entered episodes, and 5 total interruptions. The evidence rejects this intervention as an actionable route toward 196/200 and shows that the braking penalties overwhelmed or misdirected reach learning rather than selectively correcting the transient boundary regime. The next discriminating intervention is a reach-preserving staged or substantially weaker braking curriculum: first recover T1-like approach and entry behavior, then ramp a boundary penalty only after reliable entry, while keeping complete uninterrupted success as the evaluation criterion.
request.reason: The closure condition is satisfied by a controlled fresh candidate, paired shared-seed official-distribution evaluation, and all required outcome diagnostics. T2 lost every discordant episode to T1 and failed before the boundary-regulation phase, so further measurement within I2 cannot distinguish braking efficacy from the intervention's gross suppression of reaching. I2 is therefore closed negatively; the consequential remaining question belongs to a new inquiry about reach-preserving curriculum or penalty scaling, not additional I2 comparison.
